> Also it feels weird to have uv offset vector on the node but not uv scale as it's arguably often more useful

The point of `scale_uv` is to maintain uniform texel size. `uv_offset` is meant to fix any issues of textures cutting off and misalignments.

I figured uv scaling didn't have a place in this because:
 - We would only want scaling to be uniform, and not per axis, as that would lead to deformed textures.
 - A uniform scale can be applied on the material.
 - It would add more steps to CSGBox generation.
 
I think a `float uv_scaling` that scales all the UVs uniformly could make sense when trying to fit textures that were meant for a different resolution. I've seen Kenneys prototype textures and they are 1K with 1024x1024 written on them, so it would make sense if you are going for a different scale.

I'm trying to think of a situation where `uv_scaling` would be useful other than that. If you had rectangular textures that would still be better to fix from material uv, since then you could swap that with a square texture material at any point.

I made [this proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12745) for retaining uv faces orientation within a `CSGCombiner`, and it seems your `scale_uv` option would fix what I had to use a triplanar shader for! The other part of getting the same result after combining seems would be retaining UV rotation. Do you think it would be doable with changes similar to what you've added for the scale? Or would it need different changes somewhere else in the combiner?

> I made [this proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12745) for retaining uv faces orientation within a `CSGCombiner`, and it seems your `scale_uv` option would fix what I had to use a triplanar shader for! `CSGCombiner` goes outside the scope of this PR, this just UV unwraps the faces of CSG meshes correctly, taking into account their size. The objective is to not have to use triplanar materials anymore. A localspace triplanar material works on the instance of a mesh, a vertex shader calculates the angles of each face, and then 3 sets of textures are mixed using that information. This is very expensive, and since it's done on the GPU, the changes cannot be translated to a 3D editing software. When you combine the CSGs, the transform is lost, as the data is combined into a single mesh or set of meshes. > The other part of getting the same result after combining seems would be retaining UV rotation. Do you think it would be doable with changes similar to what you've added for the scale? Or would it need different changes somewhere else in the combiner? I don't understand what you mean. This PR changes the UVs of the **meshes**, so **rotating a mesh doesn't change it**, **neither does combining it**. you can see here how I rotated the CSGCylinder: If you wanted worldspace triplanar then that would be a problem. We would need to override the transform methods of CSGs to call `_make_dirty()`, and that would make it so that the mesh gets rebuilt every time it is moved or rotated, which would have a terrible performance cost. A solution would be to alter the method for boolean operation, check a property, and calculate triplanar UVs there. This would only work with children of CSGCombiner and most of the UVs would be mismatching since they would be per face rather than per pixel. That also goes outside the scope of this PR and would need it's own proposal. ----- Reading your proposal, it would seem this PR solves it, although because it removes triplanar materials from the workflow. Should I add it to the list of proposals closed by this PR?
Ohhh right, I was sidetracked by issues that come with triplanar while it was only used as a workaround for scaling. So yes it can be closed! Thank you

> Tested locally, it works as expected. > > I think this has a lot of potential, but we need to make sure we get the UX on properties right (while keeping the compatibility constraints in mind). I'd appreciate more reviews from @godotengine/usability, as well as anyone versed in level design. Thanks for testing it. > Some feedback: > > - Top Material and Bottom Material should be in the Material section of the inspector. Right now, they are outside and therefore don't collapse if you collapse the Material section: > > > I had the editor in unfold everything mode. I was wondering why those 2 were bigger. > > - Capitalization should be added to EditorPropertyNameProcessor for `uvs` -> `UVs`, below `uv2`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c53c5a1f49fa1edf97e6b570297c90a57d30a558/editor/inspector/editor_property_name_processor.cpp#L310 > I'll look into it. > - I think the Flip UVs property could do with more flexibility. Right now, textures like wooden planks may be misaligned, and you have to rotate the entire CSG node to fix this. This can be cumbersome if that CSG node has children, or an irregular shape where rotating it by 90° would lead to a different result than just rotating the UV. > > - I suggest having one enum property to rotate the UV by 90-degree increments, and another enum property to flip the U axis, the V axis, or both. As I understand it, this computation should be trivial (unlike rotating by non-90 degree increments). So, 8 enums? edit: Could you please elaborate on this? What exactly is the problem and how does your proposed solution work? The `FLIP_X` and `FLIP_y` and `FLIP_X_AND_Y` I understand, but the 90º degree increments has me confused. Do you mean on ALL faces? If I'm not mistaken, all UVs start at 0 and are shifted from there. Inverting toggles between positive and negative values on X or Y, in other words, if the UV is read from left to right it is then read from right to left, the same for Y. This has the side effect of misaligning textures, but I don't think there's a way to fix it. Rotation would also rotate around the 0 position, having a similar effect. Now, every shape has different UVs, and rotating all faces at the same time would have bad consecuences: `CSGTorus`: all faces rotate 90º. `CSGCylinder`: all the walls would be on their sides. top and bot would rotate 90º. `CSGBox`: all walls would turn on their sides. the ceiling and floor would rotate 90º. Sooo, at this point we would be talking about a property for the walls and one for the ceiling/floor? I would like it if only the ceiling and floor are rotated (less work :D). In this case, a slider of `int` for rotation would be better than an enum UX wise. For now, I'm moving `flip_uvs` to `CSGPrimitive` to reuse the code, and maybe adding the flip_x enum there. ----- > > - I'd like to see similar UV mapping options in CSGPolygon3D, so that the roof in the above example can have its tiles property scaled (they are way too large right now). I use a CSGPolygon3D for the roof as it's an easy way to create prism shapes. > > - While in Depth mode, there could be separate Top and Bottom materials like in CSGBox3D. > > I've been avoiding CSGPolygon3D because of the code's excessive nesting. I was going to do it but on a different PR at a later time. CSGPolygon3D is it's own can of worms due to the amount of options it has: - Extrude: This would seem easy at first, but we have to remember that the user can create any shape with it, so scale UV is not likely to work very well with the current system. I was thinking of giving it an alternative UV mapping like with Box that would use something like a "cube mapping", where each face is has their UVs generated based on their normal. - Spin: It's weird. - Path3D: It's very hard. On top of the shape created by the user, we have to take into account the rotation and spin of the path3D, which can coil back into a torus or do all kinds of things. The "cube mapping" would be a good solution to this problem for implementing scale_uv. I would also like to add more alternatives, like aligning the faces on the Y "direction" like with cylinder, for vertical shapes and probably for spin mode too. So as I said, it would be better if it's added as a **different PR** after we are done with this one, it would also help to have the properties frozen so I don't have to go back to each Node and adjust them like you are asking of `flip_uvs`.

> We discussed this at the animation meeting. The uv flipping needs to be a separate change.
> 
> I also think the code needed to support this and the uv flip is extremely complex and will make CSGBox3D and other shapes much more difficult to maintain.
> 

 - I agree on CSGBox, I've been looking at CSG editors like Red Faction 1 editor and Serious editor 1, and a box has more features, like divisions, twist and bend, and that would be difficult to implement with a fixed 12 faces. The original code could've been extended.
I think I can **adapt part of the UV code on this PR to work with the original Box generation code**, but I would have to start over with a different branch.

 - On CSGCylinder and CSGTorus, the UVs were broken, and the fix was made on the original code, I can't see anything wrong with it.

> Special case for top and bottom material looks useful, but I just want to be able to see if it can be done without less complexity, and the UV flip code looks complicated. It would be nice if this could be done more generally somehow.
> 

UV flip code is probably the simplest part of this PR, all it does is invert the X values of all UVs of the mesh.

This is kind of a jerry-rig, I needed these features to make levels in godot, otherwise we need to wait for someone to implement the systems to select faces and edit vertices.
But it's not difficult to extend, it affects only `_build_brush`, which generates the vertices, uv data, materials and smooth for the mesh. The mesh itself is stored as a `brush`.

line 480 of csg_shape.cpp:
```c++
CSGBrush *CSGShape3D::_get_brush() {
	if (!dirty) {
		return brush;
	}
```

If we were to add a per face or vertex editor, all we would have to do is alter this data and update the mesh.
The only problem would be that changing any values on the CSG would make the mesh dirty and reset all changes.
I've been thinking of adding a separate method to `_make_dirty` to not rebuild the entire mesh but just alter it's properties, for things like uv, or even to assign more materials to change the number of surfaces.

Another problem is that faces are stored as tris, for an editor it would be better UX wise to be able to select quads, or even ngons.

-----

So, I'm not confident on this PR any more, it has grown out of control and done too many things, and I have these ideas on how to make it better. I've learned a lot from it though.
I think we can close this and I can start over when I have some time, and open a bunch of different PRs instead:

- [x]  fix `CSGCylinder` and `CSGTorus` uvs.
- [ ] change UVs of `CSGBox` and add `compatibility_mode`.
- [ ] implement `scale_uv`.
- [x] implement `flip_uvs`.
- [x] add an alternative to `_make_dirty` to update `CSGBrush` instead of rebuilding it.
- [x] add methods to interact with `CSGBrush` more easily.
- [x] add quads and ngons to `CSGBrush` in preparation for a face editor and smooth groups.
